name: Emulator Hardware Indicators
description: Detects virtualized and emulated hardware environments using offscreen OpenGL ES renderers, ARM64 hardware timer registers, and scheduler jitter analysis.

evidenceUnits.title: Offscreen OpenGL ES renderer
evidenceUnits.observedObject: EGL display and OpenGL ES GL_RENDERER and GL_VENDOR strings
evidenceUnits.proposition: The offscreen OpenGL ES renderer identifies a software rasterizer or virtual machine graphics driver
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires EGL display initialization and pbuffer surface support
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Vendor strings can be spoofed in modified emulator builds
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Identifies known emulator rendering drivers; does not classify physical GPU variants

evidenceUnits.title: ARM64 hardware timer register deviation
evidenceUnits.observedObject: ARM64 cntvct_el0 and cntfrq_el0 virtual counter registers
evidenceUnits.proposition: The ARM64 virtual counter frequency or drift deviates significantly from CLOCK_MONOTONIC
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: ARM64 inline assembly instructions and POSIX monotonic clock
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Hypervisors may trap or emulate timer register reads with overhead
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Indicates virtualized counter timing characteristics; does not pinpoint hypervisor vendor

evidenceUnits.title: Scheduler yield jitter distribution
evidenceUnits.observedObject: POSIX sched_yield latency distribution across 32 iterations
evidenceUnits.proposition: The thread yield latency exhibits abnormally low coefficient of variation characteristic of deterministic virtualization
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires monotonic clock access and thread scheduling privileges
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Physical system quiescence may occasionally reduce scheduling jitter
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: Statistical heuristic indicating virtualization; requires correlation with hardware signals
